question.title: Make UTF-8 mode default
caller: Python application authors using implicit text encodings
Users configuring Python startup and compatibility behavior
input: UTF-8 text files, stdio, pipes, and filesystem paths
PYTHONUTF8, -X utf8, PYTHONIOENCODING, and optional explicit encoding="locale"
output: Consistent UTF-8 defaults across the listed I/O surfaces
Locale-module behavior unaffected by UTF-8 mode
Preserved opt-outs and explicit locale-based reads for compatibility
limits: The first draft targets Python-Version 3.12 and says its mode change may arrive in 3.11 if possible; the latter is a preference, not a requirement.
The first draft requires locale.getpreferredencoding()/locale to be unaffected by UTF-8 mode; do not substitute later PEP behavior.
Existing non-UTF-8 implicit inputs can fail or corrupt text; compatibility controls are part of the boundary.
The first Created field is XX-Mar-2022; publication date comes from PR #2443, not from repairing that placeholder.

whole_must.predicate: Python starts with UTF-8 mode enabled by default, giving files, stdio, and pipes consistent implicit UTF-8 encoding.

source_positions.section: Abstract; Enable UTF-8 mode by default
source_positions.excerpt:
This PEP proposes making UTF-8 mode [1]_ on by default.

With this change, Python uses UTF-8 for default encoding of files, stdio, and
pipes consistently.

whole_must.falsifying_input: Start with an ordinary non-UTF-8 locale and no UTF-8 opt-in; read/write representative non-ASCII UTF-8 text through implicit text APIs.
whole_must.failure_condition: The default remains locale-dependent or one of files/stdio/pipes uses another encoding.

whole_must.predicate: The mode affects stdio, filesystem encoding, TextIOWrapper, and the named APIs built on TextIOWrapper.

source_positions.excerpt:
After this change, UTF-8 mode affects to:

* stdio

   * User can override stdio encoding with ``PYTHONIOENCODING``.

* filesystem encoding

* ``TextIOWrapper`` and APIs using it including ``open()``,
  ``Path.read_text()``, ``subprocess.Popen(cmd, text=True)``, etc...

whole_must.falsifying_input: Exercise open(), Path.read_text(), and subprocess.Popen(..., text=True) with UTF-8 non-ASCII text under a non-UTF-8 locale.
whole_must.failure_condition: One listed I/O surface still interprets the bytes using a locale codec.

whole_must.predicate: Enabling UTF-8 mode does not override locale.getpreferredencoding() or other locale-module behavior.

source_positions.excerpt:
Currently, UTF-8 mode affects to ``locale.getpreferredencoding()``.

This PEP proposes to remove this override. UTF-8 mode will not affect to
``locale`` module.

whole_must.falsifying_input: Record the locale module’s encoding in a configured non-UTF-8 locale and enable UTF-8 mode.
whole_must.failure_condition: The mode changes that locale-module answer to UTF-8.

source_positions.excerpt:

whole_must.falsifying_input: Enable the UTF-8 default and supply a supported non-UTF-8 PYTHONIOENCODING value for stdio.

whole_must.predicate: Users can disable the UTF-8 mode with either PYTHONUTF8=0 or -X utf8=0.

source_positions.excerpt:
Enable UTF-8 mode by default
----------------------------

Python enables UTF-8 mode by default.

User can disable UTF-8 mode by setting ``PYTHONUTF8=0`` or ``-X utf8=0``.

whole_must.falsifying_input: Run separate processes with PYTHONUTF8=0 and -X utf8=0 under a non-UTF-8 locale.
whole_must.failure_condition: Either documented disable mechanism leaves UTF-8 mode enabled.

whole_must.predicate: The compatibility path allows discovery of implicit default-encoding use through EncodingWarning and explicit encoding="locale" to keep locale decoding.

source_positions.excerpt:
To resolve this backward incompatibility, users can do:

* Disable UTF-8 mode
* Use ``EncodingWarning`` to find where the default encoding is used and use
  ``encoding="locale"`` option to keep using locale encoding. [2]_

whole_must.falsifying_input: Run code with an implicit open under EncodingWarning, then read a valid locale-encoded non-UTF-8 file using encoding="locale" while UTF-8 mode is on.
whole_must.failure_condition: Implicit uses cannot be diagnosed through the stated warning facility, or explicit locale decoding is overridden by UTF-8.

candidates.name: CPython UTF-8 mode for implicit text-file I/O
candidates.proposed_use: Run ordinary open/io.open text reads under the documented UTF-8 mode so callers can decode UTF-8 files without a per-call codec.
